summary: The proposal presents a relevant integration problem and a plausible technical direction, but it is not ready for submission. Critical omissions include the required sections, bibliography length, figures, and AI transparency statement, while major weaknesses remain in the problem framing, objectives, writing, and schedule design.

findings.title: Required Introduction, Motivation, and Objective sections are missing
findings.description: The proposal lacks the required dedicated Introduction, Motivation, and Objective sections. Add an Introduction before the Problem section to establish the research context and scope; add a Motivation section explaining the importance and expected benefits of integrating Artemis with GitLab CI; and add an Objective section with a short introduction, 3–4 one-line high-level objectives as bullet points, and one subsection of at least two paragraphs for each objective. Formulate objectives with clear action verbs rather than presenting them only as combined motivation/objective text in the abstract.

locations.quote: Motivation/Objective: Since some Version Control (VC) systems include a Continuous Integration (CI) application, it is possible to **reduce the efort required to maintain the servers and migrate the CI service** from external applications as Jenkins to the inbuilt CI service.

findings.title: Too few bibliography entries
findings.description: The References section contains only five publications. Add at least one additional peer-reviewed publication to meet the minimum of six, preferably providing six to eight relevant sources.

locations.quote: **[Booch95]** Booch, G. Object-oriented analysis and design with applications (2. ed.).
**[Krusche18]** Krusche, S.; Seitz, A. ArTEMiS: An Automatic Assessment Management System for Interactive Learning.

findings.title: Fewer than two required figures
findings.description: The proposal contains only one figure, although at least two are required. Add a second meaningful figure, including at least one identifiable suitable UML diagram such as an activity, component, class, or use-case diagram; do not use a sequence diagram.

findings.title: Missing AI transparency statement
findings.description: The proposal lacks the required AI transparency statement. Add a dedicated first-person statement naming every AI tool used, explaining its purpose, identifying the sections in which it was used, and confirming that all AI-generated text was checked for correctness and coherence.

findings.title: Problem definition mixes solution proposals and omits stakeholder impacts
findings.description: The Problem section mixes the current problem with a desired solution and does not sufficiently identify affected actors or their impacts. Move proposed functionality such as changing build plans and compiler behavior to the Motivation, Requirements, or Solution section. In the Problem section, explicitly identify instructors, students, course administrators, and universities, and explain how server overhead and manual build-plan updates affect each stakeholder.

locations.quote: In exams, it would be useful to **change the student build plans after the submission date** to firstly hide the test cases during the exam and only compile the code and secondly use a debug compiler not failing due to a simple syntax error.
This leads to additional server overhead, since the CI and the Version Control (VC) are running on different servers. Particularly smaller universities might then not use Artemis.

Later changes to the base build plan are not patched automatically to all student build plans, but rather the build plans must be updated manually in the CI Server. Especially in large software engineering courses this is nearly impossible.

findings.title: Schedule is not organized around iterative, integrated, measurable increments
findings.description: Reorganize the schedule into explicitly dated 2–4 week iterations, each ending with an integrated, demonstrable increment. Replace the current horizontal component sequence with vertical end-to-end capabilities, such as configuring one exercise, executing its GitLab CI build with an Artemis-provided plan, and displaying the resulting grade in Artemis. Treat requirements as a backlog selected within each iteration rather than as a separate activity, and define measurable deliverables or acceptance criteria for every iteration, including the currently vague models, requirements, and improvements tasks.

findings.title: Several sentences use forbidden sentence starters
findings.description: Rewrite sentences that begin with forbidden subordinating or infinitive constructions so that they begin with the main subject and action, or combine them with the preceding sentence. Apply this to all cited examples, including “Since,” “To achieve this goal,” “In order to,” “As a result,” and “As described in section 3.”

locations.quote: **Since some Version Control (VC) systems include a Continuous Integration (CI) application**, it is possible to reduce the effort required to maintain the servers and migrate the CI service from external applications as Jenkins to the inbuilt CI service.
**To achieve this goal**, Artemis uses a Version Control (VC) and Continuous Integration (CI) server
**In order to implement this idea**, the lecture is split up into multiple iterations
**As a result**, instructors are able to update the build plan after the release of an exercise

**Since the benefits of using CI are quite high** and nearly half of the developers who do not use CI mention a lack of familiarity as the reason for not using a CI service, it is useful to teach the concepts of CI at university
**As described in section 3**, this might lead to better developers and better code

findings.title: API is undefined at first use
findings.description: Define “API” at its first use as “application programming interface (API)” before using the abbreviation elsewhere.

locations.quote: This system supports the provision of the build plan via the Artemis **API**

findings.title: Excessive filler transitions weaken sentence precision
findings.description: Remove filler transitions such as “Furthermore,” “Additionally,” “also,” and “In addition” where they do not express a precise logical relationship. Replace them with explicit causal, contrasting, or additive relationships when needed.

locations.quote: **Furthermore**, it should be possible to adjust the build plan after the task has been assigned.
**Additionally**, the base build plan is copied once after the student started the exercise
**Furthermore**, the CI service should be part of the VC server to reduce additional effort by maintaining two servers.
Not only projects using CI release twice as often as projects without CI, but the build is **also** less likely to fail in the master branch
**In addition**, universities will save time and money as they will need at least one less server.
**In addition**, either Ansible or a Kubernetes cluster can be used for automatic deployment of the GitLab CI Runners.

findings.title: Two Expected Findings paragraphs are underdeveloped
findings.description: Expand or combine the two short Expected Findings paragraphs so that each develops its claim sufficiently. Explain the expected nature of the university savings and why Ansible or Kubernetes is relevant to the implementation and deployment plan.

locations.quote: **In addition, universities will save time and money as they will need at least one less server.**
**In addition, either Ansible or a Kubernetes cluster can be used for automatic deployment of the GitLab CI Runners.**

findings.title: Schedule uses first-person statements
findings.description: Avoid first-person pronouns in the schedule. State the commitment impersonally or identify the thesis schedule directly.

locations.quote: During this time, **I will not have time** to work on my thesis.
Instead, **I plan to work** on my thesis for about 2 weeks during the summer holidays in August.

findings.title: Inconsistent capitalization and spelling in labels and workflow terminology
findings.description: Apply consistent title case and correct spelling in schedule labels and exercise names. Use labels such as “Prototype Implementation: Connectivity to GitLab CI,” “Prototype Implementation: Sending Build Results to Artemis,” “Documentation for Installation and Configuration of Artemis with GitLab CI,” and “Revise Models with Concrete Implementation.” Rename the exercise to “Exercise Workflow” and spell “workflow” consistently throughout.
